text:
sam-sre: FYI FinTrust auditor just pinged support asking for evidence and a remediation timeline for a reported vuln in our tokenizer lib used by private deployments (fast-tokenizer). They called out CVE-2026-0421 in their questionnaire. Can eng-sec triage?

jaya-engsec: Thanks — putting eyes on it. Do we know which components import fast-tokenizer in customer images (hosted vs dedicated vs private)?

sam-sre: Quick grep across repos shows uses in: runtime/tokenizer, tools/sync-embeddings, and private-deploy/agent. Hosted runtime doesn't bundle it directly for model inference (we use compiled tokenizers), but Dedicated and Private customers using the agent do.

olivia-cse: FinTrust is in Private (VPC) + enterprise add-on. Auditor wants: 1) SBOM evidence with version pinned, 2) vulnerability assessment (exploitability + PoC if public), 3) patch schedule and whether it's a configuration-only mitigation, 4) RBAC and KMS audit logs showing we rotated keys/limited access. Deadline: auditor follow-up on Tuesday EOD.

jaya-engsec: OK. I pulled the CVE entry. Summary: CVE-2026-0421 — out-of-bounds in fast-tokenizer <=1.2.3 leading to remote crash during crafted input stream. Public PoC posted but requires attacker-controlled input hitting agent's local gRPC endpoint (not exposed by default). Severity: CVSS 7.2 (high) per NVD.

mike-dev: Mitigations that reduce risk: disable remote tokenization stream in agent (we already default to local IPC), firewall the gRPC interface, and upgrade package to 1.2.4 which patches bounds check. I opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-agent/pull/312 (patch + test).

sam-sre: Good. For customer evidence we need: SBOM showing old vs new version, proof of upgrade for Private deployments, RBAC/KMS logs for the deploy, and a short risk statement for the auditor about exploitability in their environment.

jaya-engsec: Action plan proposal: A) classify as "high" but limited exploitability for standard deployments; B) schedule hotfix rollout for Private within 48h and Dedicated in next maintenance window (72h); C) provide mitigation guidance for customers who cannot patch immediately (iptables rule + agent config flag disable-stream = true); D) produce artifacts: SBOM diff, audit logs, PR link, test run output, and signed attestation.

olivia-cse: FinTrust wants explicit instructions to show they applied the fix in their environment too (they control their agent pod). Can we supply a one-line audit check they can run?

mike-dev: Yes — two checks: 1) SBOM CLI: `sbomctl query private-agent fast-tokenizer --json | jq -r '.packages[] | select(.name=="fast-tokenizer") | .version'` should return `1.2.4`; 2) agent config: `grep disable_stream /etc/redwood/agent.yaml` should show `disable_stream: true` if they applied mitigation.

jaya-engsec: I'll prepare the risk blurb. Draft: "CVE-2026-0421 affects fast-tokenizer <=1.2.3. Exploitation requires attacker-controlled input to the agent's tokenization gRPC interface, which is not exposed by default in Redwood Private when deployed following our hardening guide. Attack surface is limited; recommended remediation is package upgrade to 1.2.4. Temporary mitigation: set `disable_stream: true` and restrict agent port via host firewall or cloud security group."

sam-sre: Great. For RBAC/KMS evidence: we rotated deploy key and used customer-managed KMS for artifacts in this rollout. Which logs should we export?

jaya-engsec: Export these: 1) IAM policy change audit: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="SetIamPolicy" AND resource.labels.project_id="redwood-prod"' --freshness=2d` (for hosted). 2) KMS key rotation log: search audit logs for `cryptoKeyVersions.create` on key `projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/private-agent-deploy` for the rotation event. 3) CI artifact signature: see pipeline run id in PR. I'll attach the exact log snippets.

mike-dev: I added pipeline step in PR to record `sbomctl generate` output artifact and to sign packages with our KMS. The pipeline run: `https://ci.redwood.com/runs/98765` contains `sbom.json` artifact.

olivia-cse: Can you also include a short remediation timeline that we can forward to the customer? They need ETA for full patch across their fleet if they opt for us to coordinate.

jaya-engsec: Draft timeline: - 0-24h: notify customers, provide mitigation steps and SBOM diff; - 24-48h: hotfix release (private-agent 1.2.4) and automated patch job available; - 48-96h: coordinated patching windows for Private customers who request vendor assistance; - 7d: full sweeps and verification for all Dedicated clusters.

sam-sre: Sounds good. I'll assemble artifacts: SBOM diff (old->new), PR link, CI run, RBAC/KMS log snippets, and the risk statement + timeline. Will label the package upgrade as P1 (customer-facing).

mike-dev: After we push the agent release I'll post a short changelog and one-liner audit commands in the support KB. Also adding an automated compliance note to the Console to flag clusters with vulnerable versions.

jaya-engsec: I'll draft the auditor response and tag you both. Need someone to sign off on the RBAC logs before sending — @sam-sre?

sam-sre: I'll confirm and export logs by EOD.

deploy-bot: Deployment triggered for private-agent/1.2.4 to canary group (10%) — run id 98766. Status: in_progress.

olivia-cse: Thank you. I'll keep FinTrust updated and let them know we have a documented plan + evidence package incoming.

sam-sre: Final note: remind customers to rotate any ingress keys if they had custom network exposure. I'll include rotation steps and KMS evidence in the package.

jaya-engsec: Closing: compile artifacts and reply to auditor with the package link (signed tarball) + timeline. I'll QC the language for SOC2 phrasing. :white_check_mark:
